back: The route a product takes from producer to consumer, including any intermediaries.
Producer → consumer; producer → retailer → consumer; producer → wholesaler → retailer → consumer; producer → agent → (retailer) → consumer.
No intermediaries' mark-ups, close contact with customers, control over price and display.
They break bulk, store, transport and reach many small retailers a producer could not reach.
Each intermediary adds a mark-up and time; producer has less control and less customer contact.
Product type (perishable, technical), number and location of customers, producer's resources, cost, control, competitors, selling abroad.
Arranges sales for a producer, usually for commission, without owning the goods; common in foreign markets.

front: Online selling: one advantage and one drawback?
back: Advantage: reaches customers anywhere at any time. Drawback: delivery costs and customers cannot inspect goods.
Yes (direct sales, supermarket chains, online), but its functions must still be performed by someone.
